findings: PA projection chest radiograph based on visible clavicles, scapulae, and symmetrical rib configuration

Large homogeneous opacification occupying the entire left lower zone and extending into the left mid zone, with an abrupt superior margin and complete opacification of the left costophrenic angle, consistent with a large left-sided pleural effusion
The left hemidiaphragm is not visible; the right hemidiaphragm and right costophrenic angle are sharp and clearly defined
The mediastinum appears shifted slightly to the right, suggesting mass effect from the left-sided collection
The right lung demonstrates increased bronchovascular markings, particularly in the right lower and mid zones, with no focal consolidation or pleural effusion on the right
The cardiac silhouette is partially obscured on the left; the right heart border is visible
The trachea appears midline to mildly rightward deviated
No visible rib fractures, pneumothorax, or gross bony abnormality on the right; left shoulder and humeral head are intact
The left upper lobe appears aerated and relatively clear
differential: Large left pleural effusion (transudative or exudative etiology, e.g., heart failure, malignancy, parapneumonic/empyema)
Left lower lobe collapse with associated pleural effusion (combined atelectasis and fluid)
Left hemithorax opacification secondary to malignant pleural disease with effusion (e.g., mesothelioma, metastatic pleural involvement)
anatomyConcerns: Mediastinal shift to the right is present, which is consistent with a large space-occupying left pleural effusion rather than an impossible anatomical finding
The left lung parenchyma in the lower two-thirds is not assessable due to the overlying effusion opacity
Right-sided bronchovascular markings are prominent, which could reflect compensatory over-inflation or underlying vascular congestion and should be interpreted cautiously without clinical context
